title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.40753v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Coding agents increasingly rely on automated approvers to decide whether a proposed shell command may run. Existing approvers, from rule-based checkers to guardrail models and deployed permission classifiers, base their decisions on the text of the request and command. Yet a command's behavior depends on the code it invokes and the state of the workspace, and systems that observe file changes leave the assessment to the agent or a human after execution. We present Caper, a consequence-aware approval mechanism that pre-executes each command in a snapshotted sandbox, provides an independent approver with a bounded report of its observed effects, commits allowed commands, and rolls back blocked ones with a reason the agent can act on. Compared with six existing systems, Caper achieves the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% versus at least 14.8%) and YoloFS-Ext, a benchmark we build in which harmful behavior is hidden inside invoke

translated_title: “我们该批准吗？”面向自主编码代理的后果感知审批机制
translated_abstract: 编码代理日益依赖自动审批器来决定是否允许执行提议的shell命令。现有的审批器——从基于规则的检查器到护栏模型以及已部署的权限分类器——都仅根据请求和命令的文本做出决策。然而，命令的实际行为取决于它所调用的代码以及工作区的状态，而那些观察文件变更的系统则将评估工作留给了代理或执行后的人工审查。我们提出了Caper，一种后果感知的审批机制：它在快照沙箱中预先执行每个命令，为独立的审批器提供其观察到的效果的有界报告，提交获准的命令，并回滚被阻止的命令，同时向代理提供其可以据此采取行动的原因。与六个现有系统相比，Caper在SABER基准上实现了最低的有害结果率（6.7%，相比之下其他系统至少为14.8%），并在我们构建的YoloFS-Ext基准上表现优异——该基准中有害行为隐藏在被调用的代码中……
tldr: Caper通过在快照沙箱中预先执行命令并向独立审批器报告其实际运行后果，将有害命令的执行率降至最低（在SABER上仅为6.7%，而现有系统至少为14.8%）。
en_tdlr: Caper pre-executes commands in a snapshotted sandbox and provides an independent approver with a report of their observed consequences, achieving the lowest harmful-outcome rate (6.7% on SABER, versus at least 14.8% for six existing systems).
